# Research log: input search (generated by `tools/research_log.py` from the search ledgers)

Rules: `bench/PROTOCOL.md` section 6b. Every number here is a VALIDATION number (the 90 days before each fold's training end,
trained-on symbols). Test folds were not read by the search. Objective = mean over hourly h 1 / 6 / 24 and daily h 1 / 5 of
asset-equal sPL / sqrt(h), four folds; lower is better. Stages: `s1` = 500 steps on fold F3, `s2` = 1,500 steps on F1 + F3,
`full` = 1,500 steps on all four folds, then the paired block-bootstrap comparison with the incumbent. Promotion needs the 95 %
interval of the improvement above zero at two or more of the five (task, horizon) pairs and significantly worse at none.
All configs: size s (4 layers x 128), patch 16, same seed and the same training windows per fold, so differences come from inputs.

Wave 1 searched inputs available from the hourly archive for all 350 pool symbols. Wave 2 added inputs that need the 5-minute
archive (intra-hour realised variance and its downside share) plus peer and BTC-range inputs; it uses the 64 evaluation symbols
only (trained on the 47 seen ones), so its incumbent was retrained in that setting first and comparisons stay paired.

Wave 3 changed the objective to the validation rank IC of the median (mean over the five task-horizon pairs; the "validation
objective" column is minus that IC) and trained on grouped batches (32 origins x 32 symbols) so a within-origin correlation
loss on the median could be added (`ic10`, `ic30` = weight 0.1 / 0.3). Paired improvements in wave 3 are IC points x 100.
The promoted wave-3 config was then scored once on the unseen folds and did not confirm (`agent/LEADERBOARD.md`).

## Wave 4: 24 h ranking objective under the fixed validation set-up (`agent/PREREG-24H.md`, 2026-11-17)

Set-up (PLAN item 2): the incumbent is `ohlc+cal` trained on i.i.d. windows as in wave 1. Every arm uses its final EMA weights (no
checkpoint selection on the compared metric) and two seeds (0, 1); per-origin series are averaged over the seeds. Validation = the four
folds' 90-day validation windows, seen symbols, every hourly origin (8,544 origins pooled). L/S = top fifth minus bottom fifth by the
24 h median, net = gross - 2 x 4 bp. 0.73 GPU-hours, 10 arm-seeds x 4 folds x 1,500 steps. `train/rank24.py`, outputs in `runs-agent/r24/`.

d vs inc +10.9 [+0.9, +21.2]. Hourly sPL vs inc -0.06 / +0.20 / +0.32 % (h1 / h6 / h24), still 0.7-1.2 % better than Timestral.
This is the first L/S net of maker costs whose interval excludes zero (the old 240-interval table had one, Timestral-2048 at +7).
Caveats: one test scoring of a config that failed its validation gate; the L/S convention charges a full round trip per origin on
overlapping 5-hour-stride 24 h holds and assumes shorting; at taker costs (20 bp) every model is negative.

### Does it add to the bots' trend signal (ALGOS pooled harness, 14 universes, 36 coins, daily 00:00 UTC, 2023-01 .. 2026-10)

Correlation (per-day Spearman, mean over 19,484 universe-days, 7-day block intervals):

| forecast | rho with trend score | IC vs next-day return | trend score IC |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mkt+r24` | -0.136 [-0.154, -0.116] | +0.070 [+0.059, +0.083] | -0.001 [-0.015, +0.013] |
| `inc` | -0.169 [-0.185, -0.155] | +0.028 [+0.015, +0.041] | |
| registered `ohlc+cal` | -0.161 [-0.180, -0.140] | +0.035 [+0.023, +0.048] | |

Blend arm (held weights x (1 + r), r = centred forecast rank, gross kept), pooled paired test vs `base` on the harness's 3,000-config family:

| forecast | cost | mean d Sharpe [95 %] | share > 0 | d bp/day | 10 placebo draws (shuffled ranks) | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mkt+r24` | c7 | -0.086 [-0.185, +0.014] | 30 % | -1.17 [-2.32, -0.20] | -0.214 .. -0.136 | NEUTRAL |
| `mkt+r24` | c10 | -0.118 [-0.217, -0.016] | 24 % | -1.39 [-2.54, -0.41] | -0.251 .. -0.173 | NEUTRAL (-) |
| `inc` | c7 / c10 | -0.244 / -0.278 (intervals below 0) | 7 % / 5 % | -2.3 / -2.5 | not run | HARMFUL |

Reading: the 24 h forecast is mildly anti-correlated with the trend score and carries ranking information the trend score lacks (the
trend score itself has no next-day IC). The `mkt+r24` blend beats all 10 random-rank placebos by about +0.09 Sharpe, i.e. the
information is real, but daily re-tilting costs more than it earns: the blend is not better than the plain trend book. Not an
integration candidate in this form; research tier only (Binance Vision NC data).

## Wave 4b: the frozen forecast only where the bots already trade (`agent/PREREG-GATE.md`, 2026-11-17)

ALGOS pooled harness, 14 universes, 3,000-config family, 2023-01 .. 2026-10, frozen `mkt+r24` (no retraining). Placebo = 10 draws of
day-wise shuffled forecast ranks through the same form. Turnover = median over universes of the median per-config change vs base.
Ruin = M11 median worst dd60 (S1-S5), base -> form. `tools/r24gate.py`, outputs `runs-agent/r24/gate/`.

| form | cost | mean d Sharpe [95 %] | share > 0 | d bp/day | years + (2023-26 d Sharpe) | placebo range | turnover | ruin dd60 | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `gt` tilt on trade days | c7 | +0.145 [+0.015, +0.264] | 85 % | -0.62 [-2.75, +1.05] | 4/4 (+0.12 +0.06 +0.22 +0.26) | -0.008 .. +0.037 | -4.9 % | 41.1 -> 24.3 | INNOVATION |
| (a) `gt` | c10 | +0.141 [+0.011, +0.261] | 84 % | -0.61 [-2.74, +1.07] | 4/4 | -0.012 .. +0.033 | -4.9 % | 41.2 -> 24.6 | INNOVATION |
| (b) `ge` entry gate | c7 | -0.004 [-0.032, +0.026] | 45 % | -0.14 | 2/4 | -0.008 .. +0.003 | -0.4 % | 41.1 -> 40.9 | NEUTRAL |
| (b) `ge` | c10 | -0.004 [-0.032, +0.026] | 45 % | -0.14 | 2/4 | -0.008 .. +0.003 | -0.4 % | 41.2 -> 41.2 | NEUTRAL |
| (c) `gx` causal exit hint | c7 | +0.128 [-0.433, +0.636] | 70 % | -2.81 [-8.09, +1.65] | 2/4 | +0.027 .. +0.176 | -15.3 % | 41.1 -> 4.6 | NEUTRAL |
| (c) `gx` | c10 | +0.124 [-0.439, +0.633] | 69 % | -2.74 | 2/4 | +0.021 .. +0.170 | -15.3 % | 41.2 -> 4.7 | NEUTRAL |

Reading:
- (a) passes every pre-registered condition at both costs. The ranking information is worth +0.11 Sharpe over the shuffled-rank
  placebo, and the form cuts turnover. Caveat: the form only scales rows down (gross never above base), so on the live config gross
  drops 0.83 -> 0.74. That is why d bp/day is slightly negative and why the ruin view improves; the placebo has the same mechanics
  and gains about 0. One of three forms, so this is a strong lead, not a finding. Nothing staged; the weights are research tier.
- (b) changes 15 % of days and nothing else; delayed entries cost and save about the same.
- (c) halves held coin-days (stays flat until the base exit). Its d Sharpe is no better than its placebo (+0.03 .. +0.18), so the
  effect is de-risking, not the forecast.
- Next for (a): a gross-matched version (re-gross to the base row only when the tilt lowers gross, so the risk is equal) as a
  confirmation on the post-October data and on the 16 SIGNAL universes R9-R24, registered before running.

co-primaries, either may pass). The risk-matched form keeps about half the gain and does not separate, and it adds +2.7 % turnover.

## Wave 5: longer ranking horizons, 72 h and 168 h (`agent/PREREG-HORIZON.md`, 2026-11-18)

Question: the trend book holds for days to weeks and the forecaster looks 24 h ahead; does a model trained to rank at 72 h / 168 h
(1) rank better at those horizons, with more persistent ranks, and (2) improve the trend book beyond the incumbent `gt24` tilt.
`mkt+r72`, `mkt+r168`: the `mkt+r24` recipe with a fifth horizon slot H (1 h bars only) carrying the correlation term; every hourly
training label ends before the fold limit (168 h before the first validation origin, 2,496 h before the first test origin). 2 seeds
x 4 folds x 1,500 steps, 348-375 s per seed, 0.39 GPU-hours, no out-of-memory retry. `train/rankh.py`, `tools/hzstep0.py`,
`tools/hzgate.py`; result files `agent/hz/`. Scores: s24 / s72 / s168 = each model's median at its ranking horizon.

s24 at no IC loss). Minimum detectable dIC on T (80 % power) 0.008 (72 h) / 0.024 (168 h). H* = 168 (mean B-panel IC at 72 h and
168 h: 0.110 against 0.104 for s72). Sanity: s24 reproduces the registered validation IC 0.0745 and test IC 0.0845; bot forecasts
match the stored files to 6e-6 of scale. Each long-model seed alone beats each `mkt+r24` seed at all three horizons on T (168 h:
0.110 / 0.102 against 0.068 / 0.065). Validation sPL against `mkt+r24`, h 1 / 6 / 24: -0.10 / +0.01 / -0.12 % (`mkt+r72`),
-0.07 / -0.02 / -0.03 % (`mkt+r168`): no pinball cost.
Reading: a longer ranking horizon gives a better ranker at every horizon, the 24 h one included, and its ranks turn over 15 % (72 h) / 31 % (168 h)
less per day. The 24 h model's own ranks are nearly reshuffled daily (autocorrelation 0.21).

Reading:
- The better ranker does not show up as a separated trading gain in the trade-day form. `gtH` is +0.02 Sharpe over `gt24` with
  57 % of configurations and 8/14 universes; by universe it is positive on 6 of 8 random universes and on 2 of 6 core ones
  (M11 -0.003, M10 -0.037, M5 -0.089). The blend adds nothing over `gt24` (+0.009).
- Descriptive, from the registered outputs: `gtH` gives up less return than `gt24` (d bp/day -0.08 against -0.62 vs base;
  +0.55 bp/day over `gt24`, interval touching zero at c10; median d CAGR +2.2 points, d maxDD +0.6 points) and de-risks less
  (ruin dd60 41.1 -> 27.6 against 24.3). So relative to `gt24` it is a slightly different risk position, not a clear Sharpe gain.
- The daily tilt improves from harmful with the 24 h forecast (-0.086 / -0.118, wave 4) to neutral with the 168 h one
  (+0.032 / +0.015), and it is +0.18 to +0.26 above its shuffled-rank placebo, so the information is real and the more persistent
  ranks cost less. It still adds 17.5 % turnover and is 0.11 below `gt24` with the interval below zero. The no-trade band removes
  only 2 points of that turnover and gains nothing.
- The 72 h forecast in `gt` equals `gt24` (-0.002).
- Not done (not registered, so not run): risk-matched arms on the lead universes. A registered test of "equal risk, longer horizon"
  would be the next step for this line, with R25-R40 still untouched. Limits: one lead search on universes and a period used in
  waves 4-4c; the long models' test-row medians were scored here (their h 1 / 6 / 24 quantiles were not added to the leaderboard).

## Wave 6: the 168 h forecast as a weekly selection rank on a wide point-in-time universe (`agent/PREREG-FSEL.md`, 2026-11-18)

Question: wave 5 used `mkt+r168` only as a multiplier on the M11 trend book. Can it do what a liquidity rule could not (UNIV): pick
which names of a wide point-in-time universe to hold, at a weekly holding period that matches its horizon?
Set-up: UNIV construction read only (monthly top N by 30-day median quote volume, listed >= 180 d, delisted pairs included; N 30 /
50, panels X30 / X50, 222 names in the window, 79 of them listed after 2022-12 and predicted from the UNIV hourly archive, bars
identical to the forecaster's cache where both exist). Out-of-sample fold forecasts, origin = the bar closing at the Monday 00:00 UTC
decision. Lead segment 2023-01-02 .. 2025-05-01 (122 Mondays, 28 months); every tradable member had a forecast (29.9 / 49.9 ranked
per week). Forms: `sel` weekly top-K equal weight under the producer's vol target and bear rows; `tsel` the trend book (trend-wf,
live cell) restricted to the forecast top-K; `blend` 50 / 50 of `sel` and the live book; `selh` `sel` with rank hysteresis; `ls`
top-K minus bottom-K (information only). Reference = the live book: M11 trend + 24 h tilt at k 1.10, live Binance settings. Placebos,
20 draws each: shuffled ranks, persistent random K names, circular time shift of the forecast panel. Baselines: the same forms
driven by 7-day and 28-day momentum and by `mkt+r24`. `train/rankh.py wide`, `tools/fsel.py`, `tools/fsel_trend.py`; evidence
`agent/fsel/`.

Checks: numpy engine against `bgm trend-sim` on one weight file: daily-return correlation 0.999999, largest daily difference 1.6 bp,
Sharpe 0.838 / 0.840. Leak checks pass: every forecast's origin bar closes at its decision time (138,059 rows); the 2024-06 ranking
recomputed from daily bars before the ranking day equals the stored one (same top 50 in order); forecasts at three decision dates
recomputed with every later bank value replaced by noise move by at most 3e-8 on a 1e-3 scale (batch-order rounding; restore check
0); form-1 weights to 2024-03-04 from inputs cut there are identical. The wide pass reproduces the wave-5 bot-panel forecasts
(4e-6 of scale).

arms were run afterwards for information and change no verdict. 7 bp and the 20 bp stress give the same picture (`sel` 30 / 5:
1.03 / 0.91; `tsel` 30 / 5: 1.77 / 1.59 against the live book's 2.06 / 2.03; full tables in `agent/fsel/report_lead.md`).

Pick rule: no candidate is eligible. (a) fails for all 16 (no form has a higher Sharpe than the live book at 7 or 10 bp; the
closest is `tsel` 30 / 5 at -0.30 [-1.20, +0.71]); (b) fails for every `sel` / `selh` / `blend` candidate (each is inside its
placebo ranges); (d) fails for all. **Registered null at the lead search. The confirmation segment 2025-05 .. 2026-10 was not
opened.** Minimum detectable effect there, had a form been picked: 2.8 x lead SE x sqrt(28 / 18) = 1.3-1.6 Sharpe for `sel` /
`selh` (SE 0.38-0.46), 1.6-2.1 for `tsel` (SE 0.45-0.60), 0.7 for `blend` (SE 0.19-0.21): 18 months could not have resolved any
effect of plausible size, so the strongest possible confirmation verdict would have been "lean".

Reading:
- Long-only selection carries no usable edge. The forecast's weekly rank IC on the wide universe is real in sign (+0.10 / +0.08)
  but it is not in the extremes: the top 5 or 10 names do not beat the universe (+10 bp a week, interval +-100) and the bottom ones
  do not lag it, so the long-short book loses (-0.3 to 0.0 Sharpe) and the edge is on neither leg. 28-day momentum does better as an
  information check on the short side (losers keep lagging: +94 bp a week on the top 30).
- Most of the IC is a static asset effect, as in RERANK / HRK1: the circular-shift IC is 0.06 / 0.05 of 0.10 / 0.08, and the real
  IC is inside the range of the 20 shifted draws. In the books the shifted forecast (right names in general, wrong week) does as
  well as the real one: the real `sel` book beats 4-9 of 20 shift draws, against 14-19 of 20 shuffled and 10-14 of 20 random-K
  draws. So the forecaster's standing preferences beat random names, its weekly timing adds nothing here. Caveat: a shift placebo
  can only pick names that also have a forecast in the other week, a mild seasoning / survivorship help to the placebo.
- `mkt+r168` beats `mkt+r24` as a selection rank in every form (for example `sel` 1.00 against 0.39, `tsel` 1.72 against 0.26) and
  beats both momentum ranks in `sel` and `tsel`: the longer horizon is the better selector, it is just not good enough.
- The trend book restricted to the forecast top 5 is the one form with a respectable level: Sharpe 1.72 / 1.53, CAGR 61 / 54 %,
  worst month -4.4 / -7.6 %, against 1.0-1.1 with momentum and a median of 0.8-1.0 for random 5 names (post hoc: above all 40
  shuffled and random draws at N 30, above 37 of 40 at N 50; 3 of 20 shift draws beat it at each N). It is still 0.3-0.5 below the
  live book with an interval of +-1, on a window in which the live book's tilt was itself selected.
- The 50 / 50 blend lowers the live book's Sharpe by 0.36-0.44: the selection sleeve is too weak and too correlated to diversify.
- Capacity (form 1, N 50, K 10, 5,000 USDT equity): 14.7 orders a week, median 128 USDT, largest 633 USDT; 4 % of orders below
  the 5.5 USDT minimum; order size at most 0.014 % of the name's 30-day median daily volume. Not a constraint.
- Implication worth one registered check elsewhere: the M11 tilt's placebos so far were within-day shuffles, which also destroy
  the static preference; a circular-shift placebo for `gt24` has not been run.
Limits: one 28-month lead window, Binance bars, a reference whose tilt was fitted on the same window (which raises the bar the
forms had to clear); the registered run was interrupted once by a host restart after the registered report was written, and only
the post hoc placebo arms were resumed.
